title: Cooldowns
summary: Time-gated actions: record when something last happened, reject attempts within the window. The backbone of ability systems, spam prevention, and rate limiting — best enforced server-side.

verification.source: Community-established pattern; consistent with Roblox security guidance

explanation.whatItIs: A timestamp bouncer: 'last time was X; window is N; come back later.'
explanation.whyItExists: Abilities need pacing; servers need spam immunity; economies need purchase throttling. Time is the simplest fair constraint.
whenToUse: Ability buttons: os.clock() stamps per player, checked on activation
Server-side rate limiting on EVERY remote
UI feedback: show remaining time (client-side mirror of the same stamps)
whenNotToUse: Where debounce suffices (blocking only re-entrancy, not pacing)
Client-only cooldowns as security — bypassable; mirror server truth
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
now = os.clock()
if now - lastUse < WINDOW then return "too soon"
lastUse = now
-- proceed
```
Server keeps the REAL stamps.
Client shows the countdown.
tips: os.clock() for gameplay timers (monotonic); os.time() is coarse seconds
Clean up stamps on PlayerRemoving to avoid table growth
Expose remaining = WINDOW - (now - lastUse) for radial UI
commonMistakes: Using tick()/Date-based math inconsistently — pick one clock
Trusting client-reported timestamps — always server stamps
Forgetting cooldown resets on respawn if that's the intended design

examples.title: Server-authoritative ability cooldown
examples.code:
-- Server Script
local lastCast = {}
local COOLDOWN = 4

remote.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player)
    local now = os.clock()
    local last = lastCast[player]
    if last and now - last < COOLDOWN then
        return   -- too soon, ignore
    end
    lastCast[player] = now

    castFireball(player)   -- the real work, server-side
end)

Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player)
    lastCast[player] = nil
end)
